CREM calibrations: 28/28
Para-positronium study: 28 CREM trajectories (27 reached the collision boundary, 1 censored by the per-event wall-clock budget, 0 not decaying, 0 numerical failures).
Photon panels are exact reference curves, not samples: the annihilation generator is a quantum prescription independent
of the classical model, and its self-consistency is checked in positronium_validation.
Collapse time = transit from a_pair to 0.005 a_pair (0.01 a0) under continuous electric-dipole radiation reaction,
measured by a second run of each seed, over 0 usable trajectories (0 observed, 0 right-censored).  Completion fraction: 0%.
  closed form            31.1235 ps  (mu^2 c^3 r0^3/(4 k^2 e^4) [1-(r/r0)^3], r0 = a_pair, r = 0.005 a_pair)
  not measured: --ground-state-floor holds the orbit at a_pair, so there is no transit from it
  Kaplan-Meier median    not reached: S(t) is still nan at nan ps
  mean of completed runs unavailable: no collapse was observed
Photon-cascade time of the quantized run (the collapse time reported before audit section 108): mean
  26079.9 +/- 2028.71 ps over 27 completed runs.  Most of it is the wait for the first photon (2|E0|) at a_pair, where the
  quantized orbit does not move; that is the emission model, not the clock.
  stopped by             0 Compton barrier (0%), 0 retardation limit (0%), 27 ground-state floor (100%)
  landed at periapsis    547.34 r* (median), range 545.118-547.511 r*
  period/light-crossing  861.023 at the stop (median), lowest 861.023 against a threshold of 150 -- values far below it mean the last photon jumped clean over the limit
  terminal radius        105835 fm (semi-major axis implied by the mean binding)
  terminal binding       0.00680285 keV
  terminal dipole-dipole 2.02425e-09 keV (zero expectation; contributes scatter, not a shift -- see README)
  annihilation W         1021.99 keV against 1022 keV at rest, i.e. -0.000665642% shifted (binding and dipole-dipole together)
  W/2 (2g line, 3g end)  510.996 keV against 510.999 keV at rest
  leading photon sampled 507.181 keV (99.2535% of W/2)
Model: full CREM mechanical integration under the active --radiation-reaction model, run until EITHER of two
independent physical limits is reached, whichever comes first: the pair's periapsis reaches the Compton barrier
(193.30 fm, where classical point-particle electrodynamics stops applying), or the osculating period/light-crossing-
time ratio drops to 150 (where the Darwin/retardation approximation breaks down; this bound tracks the pair's
angular momentum, not its radius, so it can trigger above or below the Compton barrier depending on the orbit) --
or the per-event wall-clock budget is spent (then censored, not extrapolated).  External lifetime is comparison only.
The collapse-time run uses the same limits under individual Landau-Lifshitz reaction; the closed-form remainder from where it stops
to 0.005 a_pair (~1e-6 of the total) is added.
WHAT THIS RUN REPORTS: the emission floor is ON (the default), so a THIRD limit applies and in practice is the
only one that fires -- the pair settles on the Bohr ground state and emission is gated there, because a photon has to
leave the pair in some state and the ladder has none below n=1.  The time above is therefore the CASCADE time from the
prepared level (--level 2) down to n=1.  It is NOT the classical inspiral time to the Compton barrier, and it is
NOT an annihilation lifetime: this model has no annihilation dynamics, no contact channel and no rate.  Use
--no-ground-state-floor --level 1 for the barrier-limited inspiral this program used to report by default.
Caution: the time above is a classical CASCADE time (see above). Para and ortho differ here only through the initial dipole
alignment, whose coupling is ~1e-5 of the Coulomb potential, so both channels yield the same collapse distribution while
their measured annihilation lifetimes differ by ~1000x.  The comparison is a scale reference, not a prediction.

Quasi-closed orbit (the 27 trajectories that reached the boundary):
  T of the sampled initial orbit  2.43173 +/- 0 fs
  T of the last resolved orbit    0.303966 +/- 2.7098e-12 fs
  revolutions between them        1.17665e+07 +/- 4.38353e+06
The orbit is not closed: it is an inspiral, so T shrinks as a^(3/2) while the pair sinks and no single period
describes the whole run.  T is the Kepler period 2*pi*sqrt(mu*a^3/(k e^2)) of the osculating orbit.  Every trajectory is prepared as an
EXACT circular Bohr state at a_n = n^2 a_Ps (L = n hbar and E = -R/n^2 identically, so e_0 = 0); the run ends when the pair
settles on n = 1, where the emission floor gates further radiation.  The revolution count is accumulated by the orbit-averaged integrator,
resolved and skipped orbits alike.
Note: 1 of 28 photon-cascade runs did not reach the boundary within the per-event wall-clock budget and are missing from the
  photon-cascade time; raise --crem-wallclock-budget-s to reduce censoring.  The collapse time above comes from the separate transit run.
  Simulated time covered by censored cascade runs: mean 50928.8 ps, max 50928.8 ps.
